title: Reduced vortex descriptors linking polycrystallinity in magnetic nanoparticles with polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering
authors: M. P. Adams, J. Leliaert, A. Michels, E. M. Jefremovas
abstract: Analytical vortex models reduce polarized magnetic small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) from nanoparticle ensembles to a small set of texture descriptors. In this work, we apply this reduction to micromagnetic simulations of polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers at a fixed particle size and examine how a controlled parametrization of multigrain disorder is reflected in the remanent descriptors. The particles are represented by explicit Voronoi microstructures, and intraparticle disorder is varied through the intergrain exchange coupling and anisotropy-axis coherence. Fitting each remanent magnetization state to a hyperbolic vortex model reveals a predominantly two-channel organization: the intergrain exchange coupling is associated mainly with the radial vortex profile, whereas the anisotropy-axis coherence is associated mainly with the orientational moment of the vortex-axis distribution. The normalized spin-flip SANS cross sections are accurately represented by independent fits of the analytical linear-vortex SANS expression obtained from the first-order expansion of the hyperbolic profile. The fitted orientational descriptor agrees closely with its independent real-space estimate, whereas the corresponding radial descriptors exhibit a strong global nonlinear relation. This separation identifies which information from the micromagnetic vortex textures is robustly retained by the reduced analytical representation.
summary: This work connects the structural disorder inherent in polycrystalline magnetic nanoparticles to their measurable magnetic scattering signatures using polarized SANS. By simulating iron oxide nanoflowers and applying an analytical vortex model, the authors successfully separate the physical contributions of intergrain exchange coupling and anisotropy alignment into distinct, quantifiable descriptors. This separation reveals which aspects of the complex magnetic texture are robustly captured by simplified theoretical models.
main_problem: The study aims to link the structural disorder (polycrystallinity) within magnetic nanoparticles to their measurable magnetic response as probed by polarized small-angle neutron scattering (SANS).
main_result: A two-channel organization was identified, showing that intergrain exchange coupling primarily influences the radial vortex profile, while anisotropy coherence governs the orientational moment of the vortex distribution.
method: The authors combine micromagnetic simulations using Voronoi microstructures with analytical reduction techniques to fit complex SANS data into simplified vortex descriptors.
model_or_system: The physical system is polycrystalline iron oxide nanoflowers, modeled via explicit Voronoi grain structures. The magnetic state is governed by standard micromagnetics (exchange, anisotropy, dipolar) and analyzed using hyperbolic vortex models.
key_observables:
Spin-flip SANS cross sections ($ rac{d\Sigma_{sf}}{d\Omega}$), radial vortex profile parameters ($
u$), and the orientational moment of the vortex-axis distribution ($\Lambda$).

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on reducing the complex SANS signal to a linear-vortex approximation, which simplifies the information content being analyzed.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate representative Voronoi microstructures and show how scattering observables are related to structural disorder parameters ($f$) and coupling strength ($k$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for descriptor reduction, details the micromagnetic simulation setup on Voronoi lattices, performs two independent fittings (real-space texture vs. reciprocal-space SANS), and finally separates the physical contributions of disorder parameters to these descriptors.
why_interesting:
While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the methodology involves mapping complex, high-dimensional simulated states onto a low-dimensional set of robust analytical descriptors ($
u, \Lambda$), which is analogous to dimensionality reduction techniques used in quantum many-body physics.
